posts.title: I finally am a morning workout-er
posts.description: All through my life, I've preferred working out in the evening. Nice time to chill out You're already limber Night runs hit different Now, after trying it out in the mornings, some things have changed. Compliance is higher with a morning habit than your evening mood. Strength training is easier in the mornings, runs are still nicer in the evening. Evening workouts, for me, were a result of intensity. I didn't believe in discipline/consistency then. Morning workouts are more about consistency – you can rack up progress even without a goal to working towards. Helps with a healthy, early-morning shot of cortisol & endorphin. Mornings aren't slow anymore though – I write less frequently, can't avoid outside pace.

posts.title: Chennai food and coffee
posts.description: Was in Chennai a couple of time over the last week. Visited a few places, recording for posterity: • Vinyl & Brew - Lovely manual brew from Blossom (Genetics Roasters), great space + nice vinyl collection if you’re into classic rock, jazz, and blues, nice food • Beachville - Nice hangout spot, coffee is nice, food is good too • Southwest - ok ok only • Manjal, Poes garden - great hospitality, decent food (ofc spice and oil heavy) - had chicken chettinad, mutton meatballs, bun parotta, and idiyappam

posts.title: Don't win the game
posts.description: I'm in Chennai for a day! Had my US Visa appointment early this morning. She said it was approved and I'll receive my passport in a week. Hope that goes smoothly. So, US it is this April! Interestingly, I gave an old person some money today. She was begging outside the consulate and I handed her a 10 rupees note. Usually, I don't give out alms, you never know if a person is truly helpless or just pretending. There's too much mental gymnastics in trying to ascertain it everytime. And you come across 20+ people everyday, so, you can't give to the first two but not to the third one. So, I have my rule – don't give alms on the street. But today, I did! Was it because I hoped for good karma to find me again? Was it selfish? Bowing to the insentience? Maybe. She helped a person identify the right line to get into. Not her job – I even doubt she knows what's going on inside the building she begs outside of. But she saw that people are nervous, hopeful, and care about the lines – so she learnt
